runs.title: Newsom commutes all 548 CA death sentences
runs.prompt: Today (5 November 2026), California Governor Gavin Newsom reportedly commuted the sentences of all 548 people on the state's death row to life without parole. Using only page fetches (no search), find: (1) exactly how many prisoners were affected, (2) what the commuted sentence converts to, (3) why Newsom says he did it, and (4) a direct quote from his office or the state. Start from a news homepage and follow links; prefer a source that is not paywalled.
runs.answer: (1) Exactly 548 prisoners were affected — Newsom commuted the death sentences of all 548 people on California's death row, described as the largest death row in the Western Hemisphere. (2) The death sentences were converted to life in prison without the possibility of parole. (3) Newsom says he did it because he believes state-sanctioned killing is incompatible with California's values, undermines the foundation of the legal system, and diminishes everyone; he also cited nearly 30 years of opposing executions and long-standing concerns about racial discrimination, high costs and the risk of error. (4) Direct quote from his open letter to Californians, shared by his office: "I take this action because I firmly believe that state-sanctioned killing is incompatible with California's values, undermines the foundations of our legal system, and diminishes all of us."
obstacles: None — all three provided sources loaded fully and were not paywalled; CNN was truncated but contained the key facts.

So "5 tankers + 1 tugboat" is an Iranian claim; the only independently reported strike is one tanker off Qatar. (3) UKMTO is the right official body to watch

runs.title: Royal Mail probes dumped letters in Derry
runs.prompt: Royal Mail has launched an investigation after hundreds of undelivered letters were found dumped on a road near Londonderry/Derry (5 November 2026). Using only page fetches, find: (1) roughly how many letters were found and where, (2) what Royal Mail said it would do with them, and (3) what the police and an elected official said. Report from the BBC article or equivalent non-paywalled source.
runs.answer: An estimated 600 unopened letters in total were handed in to SDLP MLA Mark H Durkan's office: a bag of hundreds found on the Mobuoy Road outside Londonderry on Wednesday, plus a further bundle found by a woman in a layby on the Victoria Road near the bank of the River Foyle. Royal Mail said: "Our teams will work to recover and process the items so they can be returned to the postal network and delivered to customers," and it has launched an investigation. The PSNI said it received a report of mail found at Mobuoy Road and that follow-up enquiries led to "the subsequent discovery and seizure of a further quantity of mail," with enquiries ongoing and officers liaising with Royal Mail. Durkan called it "an inexcusable" and "absolutely shocking" situation, said he understood other similar bags were strewn around the area, warned the letters (from health trusts, government departments and banks) may contain confidential information people are waiting on, and demanded "a full investigation into this appalling situation, proper accountability."
